parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs a strongly protective state layer with a hostile national border and custody regime. Every trans visitor passes through national entry screening that now requires birth-assigned sex on passports, has halted X markers, instructs visa officers to refuse cases on 'reasonable doubt' about sex, and carries a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility — a universal-exposure measure with documented confiscations, strandings, detentions of foreign nationals, and abusive national immigration custody. Inside the state, by contrast, anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations and health care, hate-crime enhancements operate, a court enforced them in 2026, X licences exist, and 88% of residents support protections. Exposures for adults are administrative (refusal, stranding, humiliation) rather than imprisonment; a travelling trans minor loses care continuity under the January 2026 ban with provider liability, and the sports ban is unresolved. This sits in the upper Elevated/Reduced boundary: serious, universal border exposure, but strong documented in-state protection and no custodial pathway for being trans in this state.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas must show birth-assigned sex; X processing halted Feb 2025; visa officers directed to refuse on document or 'reasonable doubt' sex discrepancies; wilful misrepresentation can trigger permanent fraud ineligibility. Travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and strandings; allied governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; passport policy under active court challenge; legal-aid documentation FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: National entry screening applies at every crossing regardless of the protective state layer; cannot be avoided by choosing this state.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse. National corrections bureau adopted 2026 policies described as conversion therapy for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal); trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented at state level for national custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visa refusal, fraud investigation or removal routes the visitor into national custody regimes where state protections do not reach.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National facilities ban excludes trans people from congruent access in federally controlled single-sex spaces (airports, federal buildings) under the 2025 executive order.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no mapped facilities ban; public-accommodations anti-discrimination covers gender identity since 2018/2020; state buildings fall under protective state law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Traveller faces congruent access in state spaces but binary-sex rules in national spaces within the same trip.

care_services.exposure: State bans (Aug 2025, effective Jan 2026) prohibit puberty blockers, hormones and chest surgery for under-18s, with provider discipline and a private right of action; grandfather clause covers only treatment under way on 1 Jan 2026, not an arriving visitor minor. National insurance restrictions proposed.
care_services.protection: State anti-discrimination law covers health care since 2020; adult gender-affirming care is not restricted by any documented state provision; conversion-therapy ban on minors since 2019.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family cannot maintain a trans minor's care; a care-seeking minor can become a documented-inquiry subject via national hospital record subpoenas.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 2025 orders frame minors' care as mutilation, direct prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, and hospital record subpoenas for under-19s — state threat-framing language at national level.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State law enforcement operates under the state civil-rights statute; panic defence abolished 2024; hate-crime enhancements in force since 2019.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State police are not bound by federal directives, but federal investigative authority over speech, schools and health data operates statewide.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban forces care denial for a travelling trans minor with provider liability; sports ban for grades 5–12 exists but is stayed and its operative status unresolved; national orders criminalise facilitation of minor transition.
minors_guardians.protection: State high court ruled 3-1 in Aug 2024 protecting transgender students on privacy/autonomy grounds; anti-bullying statute covers gender identity; guardians are not defendants under the care ban as documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian accompanying a trans minor carries care-interruption exposure and ambient federal scrutiny despite protective state school law.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025, second-highest raw count nationally but published without a per-capita denominator, so rate cannot be established; attributed 'least safe in the region' characterisation is unmeasured.
street_violence_police_response.protection: July 2026 county superior court found a civil-rights violation for striking a trans woman — enforcement demonstrably works; 88% resident support for protections; hate-crime enhancements operative.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State police and courts function as recourse; the national hostile climate remains ambient background.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Sports-ban operative status unresolved; injunction status of the 2025 minor-care laws unknown; passport litigation and national health-rule proposals pending; further targeting bills pending nationally and in other states.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation against passport policy ongoing; state remedies (courts, civil-rights statute) documented as functioning; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A traveller's exposure depends on which national measures are operative at the moment of travel; unresolved items are open questions, not exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: The national entry regime resembles 0.55-B's extended secondary screening with discretionary refusal, but is somewhat harsher: documented passport confiscations, strandings, a possible lifetime fraud bar, and foreign-government advisories. In-state protections (working civil-rights enforcement, hate-crime law) are stronger than 0.55-B's remedies, roughly balancing to a similar or slightly higher level.

The state layer matches 0.75-C's protective framework: trained recourse, functioning tribunals/courts, administrative rather than criminal outcomes. But 0.75-C assumes border officers trained on respectful inspection, whereas the documented national regime mandates birth-sex documents, refusals on 'reasonable doubt', and records abusive custody — so the combined regime sits below 0.75-C.

The national visa cable's case-note tagging and refusal instruction echoes 0.35-A's universal register, but is materially narrower: it targets suspected misrepresentation and athletic visas, requires four fraud elements, allows waivers, and is contested in court — not routine exclusion of every trans visitor. The protective state layer has no analogue in 0.35-A, placing this jurisdiction clearly above it.

0.25-C features birth-sex custody placement with routine assault. The documented national custody harms here (forced labour, sexual abuse of trans men, hormone removal policies) are comparable in severity, but in 0.25-C the hostile regime is the whole jurisdiction; here those harms are distant contingencies reachable only via refusal/detention, while the visited state is protective — well above 0.25-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's journey is asymmetric. At the border, national law imposes a universal-exposure document regime: birth-assigned sex markers, halted X processing, refusal instructions for sex discrepancies, and a latent lifetime fraud bar — with confiscations, strandings, detentions of foreign nationals, and abusive national immigration custody documented. Those are tier-1/tier-2 national exposures no state law reaches. Once inside this state, the operative regime flips protective: public-accommodations and health-care anti-discrimination since 2018–2020, hate-crime enhancements, panic defence abolished, and a 2026 court enforcement showing remedies work; no facilities ban applies, and adult care is unrestricted. The worst state-layer residue falls on travelling families: the January 2026 minor-care ban (with provider liability and grandfather clause excluding arriving visitors) denies care continuity for a trans minor, and the sports ban is unresolved. National 'gender ideology' threat-framing adds ambient exposure but does not, on this record, translate into custodial risk for a visitor to this state. Net: consequential but administrative border exposure plus strong in-state protection places the jurisdiction just above mid-scale, in the low Reduced Risk range.
